description: Hot stone in a tortoise's shape, orange banked in every seam. Still keeping a crossing that stopped being used.
lore: Of the ways over the gorge, at least one is no longer taken. The path up to it went somewhere else in a Turn, the walk round came out shorter than the walk up, and the crossing has carried nothing but weather since. There is a tortoise on it, made of hot stone, old past estimating. It does not hurry and it does not give chase, and a great deal goes past it with nothing happening at all. Some things do not. When one of those comes along, the seams in the shell come up bright all the way over the skull, and by then it is generally too late to have wanted the other route.

It was never posted there. The guards on the crossings people still use are the ordinary sad kind — a shape still doing a duty that outlived whoever gave it — and this one gets filed in with them at a glance and does not belong in the file. What put it on that ledge was the picture. For a long stretch of years, everybody who described a high crossing also described what waits on one, and the versions agreed better than the describers would have admitted: something old, something slow, something you do not argue with. Then the crossing emptied and the describing carried on without it, and all that attention had nothing left to attach to. It came up out of the ground into the gap and took the post. There is no duty in it and nothing owed to anyone. There is an expectation being met, in stone, by a thing with no idea it is meeting one.

Plates shed off it as the fire underneath them cools — black glass, mostly, and now and then one comes away whole in the shape of an egg. Nothing has ever hatched out of one. Nothing was going to: an old tortoise with a clutch under it is part of the picture people brought here, and this is that picture the whole way down, eggs included. There is one real egg and it is at the middle. Crack the shell and the rest of it slumps and runs and goes out, and what is sitting in the cooling puddle when it stops is charred black, split open by live orange, and too warm to be sensible about carrying. Set against a blade it does the one thing the whole shape was ever full of: what you strike goes on burning after you have stopped. The orange itself is the harder question. It runs through shell and skull alike, and it is the stone of the stretch of massif that is the wrong colour and warm to stand on, a very long way down and a long way off. How a piece of that ground came to be holding a crossing this high, and whether it walked here, has no answer anybody trusts.
